text:
infra-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: Fabric heartbeat jitter detected across rack-7 (mlx5) — multiple QP timeouts observed, some serving pods reporting CUDA OOMs. Auto-fallback engaged for a subset of routes. Paging oncall.

oncall-sre-amy: acked. I’m on it, grabbing logs and current impact numbers.

dmitri: seeing lots of retransmits on the IB counters — ifconfig shows interface counters incrementing rx_err and drops. Also noticed kvcache RPC latencies spike in the last 90s.

raj: note: a few containers restarted with exit reason "cuda: out of memory" around 10:03 UTC. Suspect cross-node KV cache pressure + packet loss causing extra memory churn.

katie: customer metric stream: error rate for text-gen routes jumped to 11.8% at 10:05 UTC, p95 latency up 2.3x. Region eu-west-2 most affected (approx 42% of failures). Top impacted customer orgs: acme-data, pixlapps (CS alerted).

oncall-sre-amy: mitigation plan: 1) throttle inter-node KVC sync, 2) shift traffic for critical routes to local-only replicas, 3) reduce max_batch_size on affected model to lower memory pressure. Executing now.

dmitri: commands I ran:
```
# check IB link status
ibstat -l
# show counters for port 1
perfquery -x -L 1
# kubeops: mark nodes unschedulable
kubectl cordon gpu-node-73 gpu-node-74
# drain low-priority pods on those nodes
kubectl drain gpu-node-73 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

oncall-sre-amy: cordoned gpu-node-73/74. Starting drains. Reducing kvcache sync workers to 2 (temporarily).

raj: I pushed a runtime patch to serving: set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 for replicaset gpt-embed-v2 in eu-west-2 to reduce per-pod memory footprint. Rolling update in progress.

katie: monitoring effects: after throttles & batch reduction, error rate dropped from 11.8% -> 6.1% in 3m, latency p95 fell by ~30%. Still seeing occasional OOMs (2-3 pods).

oncall-sre-amy: sequence: (a) throttle kvcache sync, (b) move critical routes to local replicas, (c) apply batch-size reduction, (d) cordon nodes with highest rx_err, (e) request infra to restart mlx driver on selected hosts if counters don't improve.

dmitri: driver restart plan: schedule rolling mlx5 restart on nodes gpu-node-71..76 during this incident window. If kernel module unload fails, fallback to NIC reset via ethtool.

customer-success-bot: CS note: opened tickets for acme-data and pixlapps, informing them of degraded API success rate and ongoing mitigations.

raj: discovered one NIC with sustained port flaps — logs show "qp timeout" events correlating to container OOM timestamps. I've isolated the host (gpu-node-74) and moved its pods.

oncall-sre-amy: good. Can you also capture dmesg + nvml logs from the restarted containers and upload to the incident log? Use the snippet:
```
kubectl logs <pod> -c runtime --since=30m > /tmp/pod-runtime.log
dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > /tmp/nvml-mem.log
```

dmitri: collected and uploaded logs to /incidents/3425001234/artifacts. Looked like small allocations + fragmentation preceeding OOMs.

oncall-sre-amy: infra team, what's the status on NIC driver restart?

dmitri: started rolling restart on gpu-node-71,72. So far node72 showed improvement in IB counters after module reload. Node74 (problematic) scheduled next.

ben: taking next-hand-off at 10:17 UTC. Summary for handoff: fabric heartbeat jitter -> QP timeouts -> kvcache stalls -> extra memory churn -> 10% error rate peak -> mitigations applied (throttle sync, local route shift, batch-size reduction, node cordon/drain, driver restarts). Customer impact: degraded success rate and elevated latency, targeted customers alerted. Remaining tasks: finish NIC restarts for nodes 71-76, monitor for residual OOMs, collect postmortem evidence (perf counters, dmesg, nvml).

oncall-sre-amy: handing off to @ben now. I’ll stay reachable for escalation. Please keep the incident channel updated with any new pod restarts or customer escalations.

ben: ack. I’ll coordinate the remaining rollout and start a timeline doc for postmortem. Tentative severity: Sev2 given sustained customer impact and partial degradation.

customer-success-bot: CS updated tickets with handoff summary and expected follow-ups.

oncall-sre-amy: adding action items for postmortem: 1) correlate qp timeout timestamps with pod OOM times, 2) evaluate kv sync backoff logic to avoid mem churn on transient loss, 3) revisit k8s eviction thresholds for GPU pods, 4) update runbook for IB driver restarts.

ben: noted. Will assign owners. Final note: if we see another spike >8% error rate revert traffic to fallback (model-local) and consider temporary global autoscaling increase for dedicated capacity.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: error rate stabilized at 3.4% as of 10:28 UTC, p95 down to 1.2x baseline. All scheduled restarts completed for nodes 71..76. No new OOMs in last 6m. Continuing watch.

oncall-sre-amy: closing pager for now, keeping channel open for 30m watch. Thanks all :thumbsup:
